chunks: Faḍālah narrated from Abān, from a man, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him: How is the pledge dealt with regarding what it contains, if it is an animal, a riding beast, silver, or goods, and a fire or thieves strike it, so his property is destroyed or his goods are diminished, and he has no evidence for his loss?
He said: If all of his goods are gone and nothing is found remaining for him, then there is nothing against him.
He said: But if he says, 'It went from among my property,' while he still has property, then he is not to be believed.

key_terms.الرَّهْنُ: collateral or pledged property held as security
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal evidence or proof supporting the claim
key_terms.حَرِيقٌ: fire causing destruction of the property
key_terms.حَيَوَانًا: an animal given as pledged property
key_terms.فَلَا يُصَدَّقُ: his claim is not accepted as truthful
key_terms.فِضَّةً: silver included among forms of collateral
key_terms.لُصُوصٌ: thieves whose theft is claimed as the cause of loss

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on collateral property that is claimed to have been destroyed by fire or theft without evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning pledged property when it is allegedly destroyed or diminished by fire or theft. If a person's entire property is lost, he is not held liable; but if he claims loss from among his property while other property remains, his claim is not accepted without proof.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4112 - Fadalah narrated from Aban, who narrated from a man, that Abu Abdillah (as) was asked:

"How does the collateral (rahn) remain valid in cases where it is an animal, a mount, silver, or goods, and it gets destroyed due to fire or theft, causing the owner's loss or a decrease in its value, and there is no evidence to support the claim of loss?"
Imam (as) said: "If all of his goods are completely destroyed and nothing remains, then there is nothing (no liability) upon him."
Imam (as) further said: "However, if he claims that the loss occurred from among his possessions while he still possesses other property, he will not be believed."
